sections.heading: Pros
sections.text:
Incredibly long and very forgiving burst window, allowing dodging, mistakes, and switching if desired,

 Main Combo combines ground and aerial combat which can sometimes allow Xiangli Yao to avoid attacks mid-combo increasing his safety even without dodging,

 Incredibly powerful amplification options via team building lead to big opportunities during his ultimate burst window - stacking Verina + Yinlin outros right before ultimate is very potent,

 Has great energy and concerto efficiency between his high-generation main combo and incredibly spammable standard Resonance Skill and Forte: Resonance skill (Outside of Ultimate) abilities,

 Gains interruption resistance (not immunity) during his Ultimate state (Intuition) which should be most of his field time,

 He's free at the time of his release!

sections.heading: Cons
sections.text:
Main combo takes some getting used to, to pull off in the heat of combat but is manageable when you learn how,

 All main combo animations are very long leaving Xiangli Yao vulnerable to taking damage (even if he is rarely interrupted).

sections.heading: Review
sections.text:
Xiangli Yao is a 5-star Electro Gauntlet wielder who specializes in unleashing strong combos during his Ultimate burst window. What sets him apart from other Ultimate-focused characters, is his unusually long burst duration. This generous window allows for Dodging, Swapping, and even a few mistakes, making his gameplay more forgiving and accessible. Additionally, Xiangli Yao gains Interruption Resistance while his Ultimate buff is active, eliminating one of the most frustrating issues faced by burst-centric characters: being interrupted mid-combo. This resistance significantly reduces his reliance on Swap-Cancels—a challenge that troubles some of his counterparts like Calcharo. To better grasp his abilities and unlock his full potential, let’s dive into his kit.
 As an Ultimate-centric character, Xiangli Yao largely overlooks his non-Ultimate abilities in favor of quickly gaining access to his Ultimate. However, there is one exception - the Resonance Skill: Deduction. This ability delivers an Electro attack that generates a substantial amount of Concerto/Resonance energy, is Swap-Cancellable, and has an impressively short cooldown of just 5 seconds. Xiangli Yao's main combo falls slightly short of producing the required 100 Concerto to consistently execute his Outro. To bridge this gap, weaving in one or two uses of Deduction during your team’s rotations is highly advised. This not only ensures smooth combo execution but also contributes to additional Resonance energy.
 Xiangli Yao’s Ultimate Cognition Model is heart of his kit. Upon activation, Xiangli Yao summons a large cube projection, delivering substantial Electro damage while generating a significant amount of Concerto and placing him into the Intuition buffed state for 24 seconds. During this phase, all his abilities—Basic Attack, Resonance Skill, Dodge Counter, Heavy Attack, and Mid-Air Attack—are enhanced, alongside his Forte gauge. One of the key elements introduced by the Ultimate is the acquisition of 3 charges of Hypercube - it's a unique resource that fuels a powerful attack - Law of Reigns.
 Your goal after activating Xiangli Yao’s Ultimate and entering the Intuition state is not to perform as many enhanced attacks within the 24-second duration as possible but, instead to focus on expending all 3 of his Hypercube charges on Laws of Reign as fast as possible - as doing this will lead to the most damage per second. Additionally after consuming all 3 charges of Hypercube the Intuition buffed state will end regardless of the remaining duration ready for you to recharge it and repeat the 3 cube burst combo again.
 Xiangli Yao’s Forte Gauge is up next and he actually has access to two of them - one of which is essential to his gameplay (Ultimate empowered) and the other of which can be mostly ignored (Standard).
 His first and standard Forte Gauge is active whenever his Ultimate buffed state is not and is called “Capacity”. Whenever Xiangli Yao uses his standard Resonance Skill or Basic Attacks he generates capacity rapidly and after accumulating a full Forte Gauge worth of it his Resonance Skill - Deduction is replaced with Resonance Skill - Decipher, which deals more damage and has a separate cooldown. Decipher generates the same Concerto energy and similar Resonance Energy to Deduction and doesn’t directly aid Xiangli Yao with his game plan. For this reason, the standard Forte Gauge is mostly irrelevant and can be treated as a bit of bonus damage whenever it fills. Sometimes some of your Deductions you use to generate Concerto and Resonance energy will be converted to Deciphers but you should treat them the same and still Swap-Cancel them as fast as possible to focus on his Ultimate instead.
Xiangli Yao’s second Forte Gauge can only be accessed after using his Ultimate Cognition Model and while the Intuition buff remains active. While the Ultimate enhanced Forte Gauge is in effect Xiangli Yao’s Capacity gauge is upgraded into “Performance Capacity” which converts it into a 5-point charge system that can be accumulated by landing hits with any of his Ultimate enhanced abilities.
 As mentioned earlier Xiangli Yao’s goal during his Ultimate is to consume all 3 of his Hypercube charges as fast as possible by executing 3 Laws of Reign attacks. The catch to this is that Laws of Reign requires and consumes 5 Performance Capacity charges in order to activate. This means your updated mission now is to generate 5 Performance Capacity and spend it on Laws of Reign 3 times as fast as you can. To do this you’ll want to execute the series of enhanced abilities which generates 5 Performance Capacity as fast as possible while also dealing as much damage as possible. The best combo to do this is by combining Xiangli Yao’s Ultimate enhanced Resonance Skill - Divergence to jump into the air followed by his enhanced Mid-Air Attack - Revamp, you of course want to follow this with Laws of Reign.
 Ultimate: Skill: Divergence (Builds 2 Performance Capacity)

 Forte: Mid-Air Atk: Revamp (Builds 3 Performance Capacity)

 Forte: Skill: Law of Reigns (Consumes 5 Performance Capacity)

 That’s 1 Cube down and 2 to go but there’s an issue - while the above combo is the most efficient in terms of time, damage, and resource generation Divergence has a 7-second cooldown so we can’t just spam it 3 times in a row. To solve this we need to weave in one more combo that’s the next most efficient and that is making use of Xiangli Yao’s enhanced 3-part Basic Attack combo.
 Ultimate: Basic: Pivot - Impale P1 (Builds 1 Performance Capacity)

 Ultimate: Basic: Pivot - Impale P2 (Builds 2 Performance Capacity)

 Ultimate: Basic: Pivot - Impale P3 (Builds 2 Performance Capacity)

 Forte: Skill: Law of Reigns (Consumes 5 Performance Capacity)

 After executing the Basic Attack combo the Divergence combo should be back off cooldown to use for the third and final cube. After spending your last cube the Ultimate will immediately end and you’ll be back to the start of using a few Deductions in between your other teammates abilities to generate Resonance energy and Concerto until your Ultimate is ready to go once again.
 Additionally, while performing Xiangli Yao’s Ultimate combos, you will have ample time to incorporate Dodge Counters or Character Swaps - and all generate extra Performance Capacity. Ultimate-enhanced Dodge Counters, in particular, generate 2 Performance Capacity. If these additional charges are available, you can choose to either continue with the standard combo or integrate them, thus skipping some portions of the usual Performance Capacity building sequences to accelerate the burst process.
 Xiangli Yao's Inherent Skills significantly improve his performance, providing both offensive and defensive advantages. His first inherent skill grants a stackable Electro DMG% boost whenever a Resonance skill is used, accumulating up to four stacks. Each stack provides a 5% damage increase, and the effect lasts for 8 seconds. Given that Xiangli Yao frequently employs Resonance Skills—Deduction, Decipher, Divergence, and Law of Reigns—this buff will remain active throughout most of his combo.
 The second Inherent Skill serves as a defensive tool, granting Xiangli Yao Interruption Resistance while the Intuition State is active. This ability is vital, as many of Xiangli Yao’s powerful attacks come with long animations. Without this skill, he would need to rely on Swap-Cancels, much like Calcharo. However, with this ability, Xiangli Yao can execute his attacks freely, without the constant concern of being interrupted mid-combo, allowing for smoother and uninterrupted gameplay.
 Xiangli Yao is a great Electro-damage dealer, offering a level of accessibility that surpasses many other Ultimate-buff-based characters, without compromising on raw damage potential. His versatile and well-rounded kit makes him a reliable choice, with strong team synergies available right from his release. One of his greatest advantages is his accessibility, as he is available for free for some time after his initial banner drops (during the 1.2 patch). His easy-to-learn playstyle combined with his potent damage output makes him a standout option in his role.

sections.heading: Gameplay
sections.text:
Xiangli Yao’s rotation is extremely easy and forgiving. This is because it’s centred around casting 3 Enhanced Skills in his Ultimate Stance, which lasts a whopping 24s, leaving you more than enough time to dodge, parry, or switch out if you wish to play quickswap. However, it’s worth noting that it requires at least 1 cast of his base Resonance Skill in order to get the required Concerto Energy — luckily, this happens to coincide with the activation condition for the 5P Void Thunder set effect. Hence, before using Xiangli Yao’s Ultimate, it’s always best to press his Resonance Skill and press Ultimate right afterwards (cancelling its small amount of damage, but providing the Void Typhunder Set Effect and Concerto Energy nonetheless).
 However, it’s worth noting that stacking this effect up to its maximum of two times will require two separate uses of his Resonance Skill. In more optimized rotations, this can be used to your advantage as Xiangli Yao’s base Resonance Skill only has a cooldown of 4s, which means that via weaving in his Resonance Skill prior to executing his rotation (in the middle of the rotation of one of your other characters), you can take full advantage of his Echo Set bonus on the big initial hit that occurs when casting his Ultimate.
 In any case, it’s not required to bother doing so — below we’ll detail an easy rotation that absolutely anyone can follow consistently.
 Echo Timing: Xiangli Yao’s Echo can be used at any point in his rotation or even before it thanks to his Ultimate’s really lengthy duration. The easiest time window however, is to Swap Cancel it right after casting his last Enhanced Skill (Law of Reigns).

sections.heading: Advanced Tips & Tricks
sections.text:
As we detailed in the introduction to this gameplay section, Xiangli Yao is a character that can be played in quickswap as his rotation is very flexible and almost all of his abilities make for great Swap Cancel windows. As a result, we will list an array of possible optimizations below.
 Please note that Xiangli Yao should ideally not play in quickswap playstyles if a massive Outro buff that expires on swap (such as Yinlin’s) is active on him!
 Any of Xiangli Yao’s Ultimate attacks can be consecutively Swap Cancelled (save for his first and second Basic Attacks), as all of those animations are long enough to allow him to come back in time to continue his standard rotation sequence. In the most optimized quickswap playstyles, Xiangli Yao is a character who enters in and out of the field repeatedly, in order to cast one ability progressing his rotation further, while another character who also has good Swap Cancel windows (e.g Changli) takes the spotlight in order to play 2 DPS characters at once (or even 3, although we don’t recommend that).

 Xiangli Yao’s Ultimate stance lasts long enough to entirely forfeit doing any Forte Basic Attacks if the player keeps him out of the field long enough for his skill cooldown to repeatedly come back. However, note that this will significantly extend the amount of time that it takes until he completes a full rotation.

 Nothing prevents Xiangli Yao from using his Ultimate right at the beginning of a fight in order to weave in his attacks while your other characters are busy performing their Opener rotations — this is often used in top-level Xiangli Yao speedruns (although it is extremely difficult to achieve this in a worthwhile manner for DPS).

 Xiangli Yao’s initial Ultimate cast freezes all in-game timers a bit longer than most Ultimates do (roughly an extra second during which you’re even free to switch into another character while all ingame timers are paused, similar to Augusta’s Second Ultimate timestop). This can be exploited in Quickswap, the most common case being in order to achieve 4 Death Messengers with Calcharo more consistently (by swap cancelling a Death Messenger as Xiangli Yao casts his Ultimate).

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
Lynae Yinlin - Easily Xiangli Yao's best partners. Lynae is the best choice by a landslide since she provides an almost equivalent buff to Yinlin's Outro with a much more impressive general buffing profile in the rest of her kit; Yilnlin is another easy to use partner, as she provides great off-field DMG via Coordinated Attacks, and amazing 20% Electro and 25% Liberation DMG Amplify Outro buffs. The pairings here are quite natural and effective.
 Changli - Let's be clear: we don't recommend Changli+Xiangli Yao to casual players. The pair is extremely quickswap heavy and reliant on that mechanic to deal any semblance of good damage. It will underperform drastically if you don't quickswap a ton of attacks from both characters, especially compared to Yinlin. However, if you really want to push this game's limits, this duo is one of the highest damaging in the entire game. Good luck.
 Jianxin - Good option for Xiangli Yao if you don't own the above options, as she amplifies Liberation DMG by 38% on Outro, which is a significant boost to his damage. However, Jianxin is awkward to use due to her extended field time and Energy problems. Only use her if you don't own above choices or aren't willing to quickswap.
 Yangyang - Xiangli Yao's best option that isn't a limited 5 star if you are willing to quickswap. Xiangli Yao has several windows Yangyang can use to get a lot of attacks in and effectively allow you to play two characters at once, making for a great damaging pair. No Energy problems to worry about as well, thanks to Yangyang's Outro.
 Mornye The Shorekeeper Verina - These 3 are the best generalist Supports in the game. Mornye has a special synergy with Lynae since Lynae can apply Tune Rupture/Strain for Mornye to respond to them and provide her full array of buffs, making her the best choice generally if Lynae is in use. Shorekeeper is however a close second thanks to her massive CRIT buffs and other generalist buffs, then Verina is the most accessible and still very strong option if neither are available.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
Lynae Yinlin - Easily Xiangli Yao's best partners. Lynae is the best choice by a landslide since she provides an almost equivalent buff to Yinlin's Outro with a much more impressive general buffing profile in the rest of her kit; Yilnlin is another easy to use partner, as she provides great off-field DMG via Coordinated Attacks, and amazing 20% Electro and 25% Liberation DMG Amplify Outro buffs. The pairings here are quite natural and effective.
 Changli - Let's be clear: we don't recommend Changli+Xiangli Yao to casual players. The pair is extremely quickswap heavy and reliant on that mechanic to deal any semblance of good damage. It will underperform drastically if you don't quickswap a ton of attacks from both characters, especially compared to Yinlin. However, if you really want to push this game's limits, this duo is one of the highest damaging in the entire game. Good luck.
 Jianxin - Good option for Xiangli Yao if you don't own the above options, as she amplifies Liberation DMG by 38% on Outro, which is a significant boost to his damage. However, Jianxin is awkward to use due to her extended field time and Energy problems. Only use her if you don't own above choices or aren't willing to quickswap.
 Yangyang - Xiangli Yao's best option that isn't a limited 5 star if you are willing to quickswap. Xiangli Yao has several windows Yangyang can use to get a lot of attacks in and effectively allow you to play two characters at once, making for a great damaging pair. No Energy problems to worry about as well, thanks to Yangyang's Outro.
 Mornye The Shorekeeper Verina - These 3 are the best generalist Supports in the game. Mornye has a special synergy with Lynae since Lynae can apply Tune Rupture/Strain for Mornye to respond to them and provide her full array of buffs, making her the best choice generally if Lynae is in use. Shorekeeper is however a close second thanks to her massive CRIT buffs and other generalist buffs, then Verina is the most accessible and still very strong option if neither are available.

 Pros & Cons
 Pros
 Incredibly long and very forgiving burst window, allowing dodging, mistakes, and switching if desired,

 Main Combo combines ground and aerial combat which can sometimes allow Xiangli Yao to avoid attacks mid-combo increasing his safety even without dodging,

 Incredibly powerful amplification options via team building lead to big opportunities during his ultimate burst window - stacking Verina + Yinlin outros right before ultimate is very potent,

 Has great energy and concerto efficiency between his high-generation main combo and incredibly spammable standard Resonance Skill and Forte: Resonance skill (Outside of Ultimate) abilities,

 Gains interruption resistance (not immunity) during his Ultimate state (Intuition) which should be most of his field time,

 He's free at the time of his release!

 All main combo animations are very long leaving Xiangli Yao vulnerable to taking damage (even if he is rarely interrupted).

 Review
 Xiangli Yao is a 5-star Electro Gauntlet wielder who specializes in unleashing strong combos during his Ultimate burst window. What sets him apart from other Ultimate-focused characters, is his unusually long burst duration. This generous window allows for Dodging, Swapping, and even a few mistakes, making his gameplay more forgiving and accessible. Additionally, Xiangli Yao gains Interruption Resistance while his Ultimate buff is active, eliminating one of the most frustrating issues faced by burst-centric characters: being interrupted mid-combo. This resistance significantly reduces his reliance on Swap-Cancels—a challenge that troubles some of his counterparts like Calcharo. To better grasp his abilities and unlock his full potential, let’s dive into his kit.
 As an Ultimate-centric character, Xiangli Yao largely overlooks his non-Ultimate abilities in favor of quickly gaining access to his Ultimate. However, there is one exception - the Resonance Skill: Deduction. This ability delivers an Electro attack that generates a substantial amount of Concerto/Resonance energy, is Swap-Cancellable, and has an impressively short cooldown of just 5 seconds. Xiangli Yao's main combo falls slightly short of producing the required 100 Concerto to consistently execute his Outro. To bridge this gap, weaving in one or two uses of Deduction during your team’s rotations is highly advised. This not only ensures smooth combo execution but also contributes to additional Resonance energy.
 Xiangli Yao’s Ultimate Cognition Model is heart of his kit. Upon activation, Xiangli Yao summons a large cube projection, delivering substantial Electro damage while generating a significant amount of Concerto and placing him into the Intuition buffed state for 24 seconds. During this phase, all his abilities—Basic Attack, Resonance Skill, Dodge Counter, Heavy Attack, and Mid-Air Attack—are enhanced, alongside his Forte gauge. One of the key elements introduced by the Ultimate is the acquisition of 3 charges of Hypercube - it's a unique resource that fuels a powerful attack - Law of Reigns.
 Your goal after activating Xiangli Yao’s Ultimate and entering the Intuition state is not to perform as many enhanced attacks within the 24-second duration as possible but, instead to focus on expending all 3 of his Hypercube charges on Laws of Reign as fast as possible - as doing this will lead to the most damage per second. Additionally after consuming all 3 charges of Hypercube the Intuition buffed state will end regardless of the remaining duration ready for you to recharge it and repeat the 3 cube burst combo again.
 Xiangli Yao’s Forte Gauge is up next and he actually has access to two of them - one of which is essential to his gameplay (Ultimate empowered) and the other of which can be mostly ignored (Standard).
 His first and standard Forte Gauge is active whenever his Ultimate buffed state is not and is called “Capacity”. Whenever Xiangli Yao uses his standard Resonance Skill or Basic Attacks he generates capacity rapidly and after accumulating a full Forte Gauge worth of it his Resonance Skill - Deduction is replaced with Resonance Skill - Decipher, which deals more damage and has a separate cooldown. Decipher generates the same Concerto energy and similar Resonance Energy to Deduction and doesn’t directly aid Xiangli Yao with his game plan. For this reason, the standard Forte Gauge is mostly irrelevant and can be treated as a bit of bonus damage whenever it fills. Sometimes some of your Deductions you use to generate Concerto and Resonance energy will be converted to Deciphers but you should treat them the same and still Swap-Cancel them as fast as possible to focus on his Ultimate instead.
Xiangli Yao’s second Forte Gauge can only be accessed after using his Ultimate Cognition Model and while the Intuition buff remains active. While the Ultimate enhanced Forte Gauge is in effect Xiangli Yao’s Capacity gauge is upgraded into “Performance Capacity” which converts it into a 5-point charge system that can be accumulated by landing hits with any of his Ultimate enhanced abilities.
 As mentioned earlier Xiangli Yao’s goal during his Ultimate is to consume all 3 of his Hypercube charges as fast as possible by executing 3 Laws of Reign attacks. The catch to this is that Laws of Reign requires and consumes 5 Performance Capacity charges in order to activate. This means your updated mission now is to generate 5 Performance Capacity and spend it on Laws of Reign 3 times as fast as you can. To do this you’ll want to execute the series of enhanced abilities which generates 5 Performance Capacity as fast as possible while also dealing as much damage as possible. The best combo to do this is by combining Xiangli Yao’s Ultimate enhanced Resonance Skill - Divergence to jump into the air followed by his enhanced Mid-Air Attack - Revamp, you of course want to follow this with Laws of Reign.
 Ultimate: Skill: Divergence (Builds 2 Performance Capacity)

 Forte: Mid-Air Atk: Revamp (Builds 3 Performance Capacity)

 Forte: Skill: Law of Reigns (Consumes 5 Performance Capacity)

 That’s 1 Cube down and 2 to go but there’s an issue - while the above combo is the most efficient in terms of time, damage, and resource generation Divergence has a 7-second cooldown so we can’t just spam it 3 times in a row. To solve this we need to weave in one more combo that’s the next most efficient and that is making use of Xiangli Yao’s enhanced 3-part Basic Attack combo.
 Ultimate: Basic: Pivot - Impale P1 (Builds 1 Performance Capacity)

 Ultimate: Basic: Pivot - Impale P2 (Builds 2 Performance Capacity)

 Ultimate: Basic: Pivot - Impale P3 (Builds 2 Performance Capacity)

 Forte: Skill: Law of Reigns (Consumes 5 Performance Capacity)

 After executing the Basic Attack combo the Divergence combo should be back off cooldown to use for the third and final cube. After spending your last cube the Ultimate will immediately end and you’ll be back to the start of using a few Deductions in between your other teammates abilities to generate Resonance energy and Concerto until your Ultimate is ready to go once again.
 Additionally, while performing Xiangli Yao’s Ultimate combos, you will have ample time to incorporate Dodge Counters or Character Swaps - and all generate extra Performance Capacity. Ultimate-enhanced Dodge Counters, in particular, generate 2 Performance Capacity. If these additional charges are available, you can choose to either continue with the standard combo or integrate them, thus skipping some portions of the usual Performance Capacity building sequences to accelerate the burst process.
 Xiangli Yao's Inherent Skills significantly improve his performance, providing both offensive and defensive advantages. His first inherent skill grants a stackable Electro DMG% boost whenever a Resonance skill is used, accumulating up to four stacks. Each stack provides a 5% damage increase, and the effect lasts for 8 seconds. Given that Xiangli Yao frequently employs Resonance Skills—Deduction, Decipher, Divergence, and Law of Reigns—this buff will remain active throughout most of his combo.
 The second Inherent Skill serves as a defensive tool, granting Xiangli Yao Interruption Resistance while the Intuition State is active. This ability is vital, as many of Xiangli Yao’s powerful attacks come with long animations. Without this skill, he would need to rely on Swap-Cancels, much like Calcharo. However, with this ability, Xiangli Yao can execute his attacks freely, without the constant concern of being interrupted mid-combo, allowing for smoother and uninterrupted gameplay.
 Xiangli Yao is a great Electro-damage dealer, offering a level of accessibility that surpasses many other Ultimate-buff-based characters, without compromising on raw damage potential. His versatile and well-rounded kit makes him a reliable choice, with strong team synergies available right from his release. One of his greatest advantages is his accessibility, as he is available for free for some time after his initial banner drops (during the 1.2 patch). His easy-to-learn playstyle combined with his potent damage output makes him a standout option in his role.

 Gameplay and teams

 Rotation
 Gameplay
 Xiangli Yao’s rotation is extremely easy and forgiving. This is because it’s centred around casting 3 Enhanced Skills in his Ultimate Stance, which lasts a whopping 24s, leaving you more than enough time to dodge, parry, or switch out if you wish to play quickswap. However, it’s worth noting that it requires at least 1 cast of his base Resonance Skill in order to get the required Concerto Energy — luckily, this happens to coincide with the activation condition for the 5P Void Thunder set effect. Hence, before using Xiangli Yao’s Ultimate, it’s always best to press his Resonance Skill and press Ultimate right afterwards (cancelling its small amount of damage, but providing the Void Typhunder Set Effect and Concerto Energy nonetheless).
 However, it’s worth noting that stacking this effect up to its maximum of two times will require two separate uses of his Resonance Skill. In more optimized rotations, this can be used to your advantage as Xiangli Yao’s base Resonance Skill only has a cooldown of 4s, which means that via weaving in his Resonance Skill prior to executing his rotation (in the middle of the rotation of one of your other characters), you can take full advantage of his Echo Set bonus on the big initial hit that occurs when casting his Ultimate.
 In any case, it’s not required to bother doing so — below we’ll detail an easy rotation that absolutely anyone can follow consistently.
 Echo Timing: Xiangli Yao’s Echo can be used at any point in his rotation or even before it thanks to his Ultimate’s really lengthy duration. The easiest time window however, is to Swap Cancel it right after casting his last Enhanced Skill (Law of Reigns).

 Advanced Tips & Tricks
 As we detailed in the introduction to this gameplay section, Xiangli Yao is a character that can be played in quickswap as his rotation is very flexible and almost all of his abilities make for great Swap Cancel windows. As a result, we will list an array of possible optimizations below.
 Please note that Xiangli Yao should ideally not play in quickswap playstyles if a massive Outro buff that expires on swap (such as Yinlin’s) is active on him!
 Any of Xiangli Yao’s Ultimate attacks can be consecutively Swap Cancelled (save for his first and second Basic Attacks), as all of those animations are long enough to allow him to come back in time to continue his standard rotation sequence. In the most optimized quickswap playstyles, Xiangli Yao is a character who enters in and out of the field repeatedly, in order to cast one ability progressing his rotation further, while another character who also has good Swap Cancel windows (e.g Changli) takes the spotlight in order to play 2 DPS characters at once (or even 3, although we don’t recommend that).

 Xiangli Yao’s Ultimate stance lasts long enough to entirely forfeit doing any Forte Basic Attacks if the player keeps him out of the field long enough for his skill cooldown to repeatedly come back. However, note that this will significantly extend the amount of time that it takes until he completes a full rotation.

 Nothing prevents Xiangli Yao from using his Ultimate right at the beginning of a fight in order to weave in his attacks while your other characters are busy performing their Opener rotations — this is often used in top-level Xiangli Yao speedruns (although it is extremely difficult to achieve this in a worthwhile manner for DPS).

 Xiangli Yao’s initial Ultimate cast freezes all in-game timers a bit longer than most Ultimates do (roughly an extra second during which you’re even free to switch into another character while all ingame timers are paused, similar to Augusta’s Second Ultimate timestop). This can be exploited in Quickswap, the most common case being in order to achieve 4 Death Messengers with Calcharo more consistently (by swap cancelling a Death Messenger as Xiangli Yao casts his Ultimate).

 Synergies
 Lynae Yinlin - Easily Xiangli Yao's best partners. Lynae is the best choice by a landslide since she provides an almost equivalent buff to Yinlin's Outro with a much more impressive general buffing profile in the rest of her kit; Yilnlin is another easy to use partner, as she provides great off-field DMG via Coordinated Attacks, and amazing 20% Electro and 25% Liberation DMG Amplify Outro buffs. The pairings here are quite natural and effective.
 Changli - Let's be clear: we don't recommend Changli+Xiangli Yao to casual players. The pair is extremely quickswap heavy and reliant on that mechanic to deal any semblance of good damage. It will underperform drastically if you don't quickswap a ton of attacks from both characters, especially compared to Yinlin. However, if you really want to push this game's limits, this duo is one of the highest damaging in the entire game. Good luck.
 Jianxin - Good option for Xiangli Yao if you don't own the above options, as she amplifies Liberation DMG by 38% on Outro, which is a significant boost to his damage. However, Jianxin is awkward to use due to her extended field time and Energy problems. Only use her if you don't own above choices or aren't willing to quickswap.
 Yangyang - Xiangli Yao's best option that isn't a limited 5 star if you are willing to quickswap. Xiangli Yao has several windows Yangyang can use to get a lot of attacks in and effectively allow you to play two characters at once, making for a great damaging pair. No Energy problems to worry about as well, thanks to Yangyang's Outro.
 Mornye The Shorekeeper Verina - These 3 are the best generalist Supports in the game. Mornye has a special synergy with Lynae since Lynae can apply Tune Rupture/Strain for Mornye to respond to them and provide her full array of buffs, making her the best choice generally if Lynae is in use. Shorekeeper is however a close second thanks to her massive CRIT buffs and other generalist buffs, then Verina is the most accessible and still very strong option if neither are available.
